name: W-spiders are symmetric under the crossing
summary: Crossing two legs of a W-spider with the fermionic crossing gives the same W-spider.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

Every term of a W-spider has at most one $|1\rangle$ among any two of its legs, so the sign of the fermionic crossing never appears: black vertices are symmetric under the crossing as well as under the [ordinary swap](../w-swap-symmetry/). In the planar W-calculus of Carette et al., where wires may not cross, this is the axiom that removes a fermionic swap between two adjacent legs of a black vertex.
parameter_notes: Shown for a W-spider with three outputs; holds for any number of legs.
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator
